question: Two children present with foot deformity. Child A has PPRP; Child B has spastic diplegic CP. Which combination of features CORRECTLY distinguishes Child A (PPRP) from Child B (CP)?

answers.text: Child A: spastic muscles, brisk DTRs, scissor gait; Child B: flaccid muscles, absent DTRs, steppage gait

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is reversed. Spasticity, brisk DTRs, and scissor gait are UMN features — that is CP (Child B). Flaccid muscles, absent DTRs, and steppage gait are LMN features — that is PPRP (Child A).

answers.text: Child A: flaccid muscles, absent DTRs, muscle wasting; Child B: spastic muscles, brisk DTRs, clonus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. PPRP = LMN lesion: flaccid paralysis, wasted muscles, hypotonia, absent DTRs, no clonus. CP = UMN lesion: spasticity, hypertonia, brisk DTRs, clonus, extensor plantar response. These are reliably discriminating features.

answers.text: Child A: non-progressive, congenital onset; Child B: progressive, infective onset in childhood

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The causation is reversed. PPRP follows poliovirus infection in early childhood (post-natal). CP arises from a brain lesion around the time of birth (peri-natal) and is non-progressive. Neither is congenital in the strict chromosomal sense.

answers.text: Child A: tendon transfers contraindicated; Child B: tendon transfers are the first-line surgery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Wrong. Tendon transfers are a cornerstone of PPRP surgery (when donor grade ≥4). In CP, tendon transfers are used but must address spasticity first; the first-line surgical approach is soft-tissue lengthening/release of spastic muscles, not tendon transfer.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the mnemonics: LMN lesion = 3 Fs (Flaccid, Fine wasting, Fasciculations, absent reflexes — PPRP); UMN lesion = HUBS (Hypertonia, Upgoing plantar, Brisk DTRs, Spasticity — CP). These discriminate the two conditions reliably.

Excellent. The LMN vs UMN distinction is the most examined comparison in neuromuscular orthopaedics: PPRP = flaccid/wasted/areflexic (anterior horn cell destroyed); CP = spastic/hypertonic/hyperreflexic (UMN pathway damaged).
